# Publication Network Maintenance (#sec-kumu-pubMap)

**Elements:** The publications (i.e. each row of the dataset because there is only one value for "Type")

**Type:** There is one type of element in the dataset, which are publications

**Tags/Element Type** The columns that are used to categorize information about the elements, can contain multiple descriptors (i.e. method, theme)

## Adding Column in linked data (#sec-kumu-pubAddColumn)

1. Add the column in the main spreadsheet
1. Refresh network map page
1. Open the hamburger menu in the top left corner and go to `fields`
1. Under Relevance > Element Types > Publication, click edit at the bottom of the list and select the added column titles
1. [Re-run metrics](#sec-kumu-pubMetrics)

## Adding Pub Type (#sec-kumu-pubAddPubType)

1. Open advanced editor

## Adding Filter Category (#sec-kumu-pubAddFilter)

## Running Updated Metrics (#sec-kumu-pubMetrics)

Once the kumu_publication_network google sheets has been updated, you will need to re-run the metrics that scale the elements according to their frequency in the dataset.

1. Refresh the Kumu Map
1. Select all button under `Connect by...`.
We want **all element types** to appear on the map.
1. Click the erlenmeyer flask icon in the bottom right corner that is labeled `Metrics`
1. Click `Social Network Analysis`
1. Choose `indegree` as the metric and click `Discover the Influencers`
1. Now deselect all buttons under `Connect by...` so that the only the publication elements appear on the map
1. Choose `indegree` and again click `Discover the Influencers`
    1. This process resets the indegree value (i.e. how many connections between elements) to zero for the publications so that they have a standard element size.
    The recalculated metrics for the other element types (method, theme, etc.) will be retained and rescaled accorting to the dataset updates.

## Advanced editor code guide (#sec-kumu-pubCode)

<details><summary>Code comments for Publication Network</summary>

```r

# The controls section is going to define all of the interactive controls of the map, including the filters and cluster connection buttons.

@controls {
  top { #Sets location of next function, text, etc.
    title { #Sets the title of the map at the top. Important for accessibility!
      value: "Developmental Psychopathology Lab Publication Network"; #the title
      text-align: center; #title alignment
      font-size: 30; #title size
    }

    filter { #sets a filter at the top of the page for publication type (which is a column in dataset)
      target: element; #this is targeting the publications
      by: "Publication Type"; #options for filtering by "Publication Type" column in the dataset
      as: buttons; #Filter appears buttons instead of a dropdown
      multiple: true; #can select multiple filters at once, i.e. book and book chapter both appear
      default: show-all; #defaults to showing all of the publications types
      font-weight: bold;
      font-size: 15;
      padding: 15; #adjusts spacing around the filter bar
    }
  }

  bottom-right { #specify location for control is bottom right
    image { #adds the devpsy logo
      src: "https://developmental-psychopathology.lab.uiowa.edu/sites/developmental-psychopathology.lab.uiowa.edu/files/2022-07/Final%20Medium%20Line%20Logo%20Small.jpeg"; #this is the link to the logo on the lab website, update this link if that changes
      height: 140;
    }
  }

  top-left { #specify controls in the top left corner
    search {} #search bar will appear in top left

    text { #text header for filters
      value: "Filter by..."; #text to appear on map
      font-weight: bold;
      font-size: 20;
      padding: 0;
    }

    filter { #This will create a filter control
      target: element; #element is each publication (because there is only one "Type" in the dataset)
      by: "Theme"; #column to filter by from dataset
      as: dropdown; #sets filter to a dropdown format
      placeholder: "Theme"; #the text that appears on the filter
      multiple: true; #allows for selecting multiple filter categories (tags)
      default: show-all; #defaults to showing all themes in dataset
      font-size: 15;
      padding: 5; #helps create visual space between filters
    }

    filter {
      target: element;
      by: "Construct";
      as: dropdown;
      placeholder: "Construct";
      multiple: true;
      default: show-all;
      font-size: 15;
      padding: 5;
    }

    filter {
      target: element;
      by: "Sample/Population";
      as: dropdown;
      placeholder: "Sample/Population";
      multiple: true;
      default: show-all;
      font-size: 15;
      padding: 5;
    }

    filter {
      target: element;
      by: "Method";
      as: dropdown;
      placeholder: "Method";
      multiple: true;
      default: show-all;
      font-size: 15;
      padding: 5;
    }

    filter {
      target: element;
      by: "Open Science";
      as: dropdown;
      placeholder: "Open Science";
      multiple: true;
      default: show-all;
      font-size: 15;
      padding: 5;
    }

    filter {
      target: element;
      by: "Year";
      as: dropdown;
      placeholder: "Publication Year";
      multiple: true;
      default: show-all;
      font-size: 15;
      padding: 5;
    }

    filter {
      target: element;
      by: "Student Author";
      as: dropdown;
      placeholder: "Student Author";
      multiple: true;
      default: show-all;
      font-size: 15;
      padding: 5;
    }
  }

  bottom { #specifies that control is appearing at the bottom
    text { #text header for connection cluster buttons
      value: "Connect by..."; #text to appear on map
      font-weight: bold;
      font-size: 20;
      padding: 0;
    }

    cluster { #this function will generate the dynamic connections between publications based on the specified columns below
      by: "Theme", "Construct", "Open Science", "Sample/Population", "Method"; #specify the columns that will define the connections 
      as: buttons; #appear as buttons
      multiple: true; #allows you to connect by multiple columns (element types/tags), i.e. both theme and construct can appear
      default: "Theme"; #sets the default connection to appear, can set to * or show-all for all clusters to appear by default
      font-weight: bold;
      font-size: 15;
    }
  }
}

#The settings are going to specify the default view settings of the map. Refer to Kumu's guide on the @settings reference to see available specification options.

@settings {
  element-size: 400; #this is a larger than default element size to help with accessible visibility
  element-font-size: 400; #larger than defauly font size (under map bubbles) to help with accessible visibility
  background-color: white; #map background is white
  font-cutoff: 1;
  layout-preset: hairball; #part of the force-directed layout (bouncy instead of a static layout)
  layout-particle-charge: 4000; #repels elements from each other to create more visual space on the map
  connection-length: 400; #forces longer connection lines to create visual space/avoid tight overlapped clusters
  element-scale: scale("indegree", 0.5, 3); #this map is scaled by the indegree metric, which is specified here; can change the range of element sizes if you want the scale more/less visually drastic
  template: 0;
  connection-curvature: 0.25; #sets slight curve to gray connection lines
  selection-color: red; #sets the colored ring that will appear on a selected element (default is red!)
  cluster: "Theme"; #his will dynamically shift as you interact with the cluster buttons on the button, don't need to edit this line ever
}

#Sets the text box popup that appears when you hover over a publication. Intended to help with accessibility/visibility
["element type"="Publication"] { #specify that popover is intended for the publications (i.e. all rows)
  popover: "#### {{label}}"; #the text that pops up is the in-text citation (which is specified in the "label" column of the dataset); the #### sets it to fourth-level header size
}

#Specify the appearance of element types that are used to connect/filter publications 
element["element type"="Method"] { #use element function to tweak specifics about the elements (here we specify how the method elements will appear)
  icon: wrench; #select icon from standard css icon list
  icon-color: white; #this is why the icon appears white
  color: transparent; #removes the default circle around element so that we can add transparent shadow behind the icon below
  border-width: 0;
  shadow-color: #CC6677; #specifies to add a shadow in this color (choose color-blind friendly colors!)
  shadow-opacity: 0.4; #set opacity of shadow
  shadow-size: 1; #sets how big the shadow border around the icon, 1 is ideal
}

element["element type"="Construct"] {
  icon: star;
  icon-color: white;
  color: transparent;
  border-width: 0;
  shadow-color: #C4451C;
  shadow-opacity: 0.4;
  shadow-size: 1;
}

element["element type"="Open Science"] {
  icon: share-alt;
  icon-color: white;
  color: transparent;
  border-width: 0;
  shadow-color: grey;
  shadow-opacity: 0.6;
  shadow-size: 1;
}

element["element type"="Sample/Population"] {
  icon: user;
  icon-color: white;
  color: transparent;
  border-width: 0;
  shadow-color: red;
  shadow-opacity: 0.4;
  shadow-size: 1;
}

element["element type"="Theme"] {
  icon: comment;
  icon-color: white;
  color: transparent;
  shadow-color: green;
  shadow-opacity: 0.4;
  shadow-size: 1;
}

#Specify that network connections lines are "undirected" so they have no arrows. Also area to specify width and color of connection lines (currently set to default)
connection {
  arrow-visibility: hidden; 
  color: grey;
  size: 6;
}

#Specify color of each type of publication (relevant for map appearance and the legend)
/* Journal Publication */
element["publication type"="journal publication"] {
  color: #0072B2;
}

/* R Package */
element["publication type"="r package"] {
  color: #009E73;
}

/* Book Chapter */
element["publication type"="book chapter"] {
  color: #E69F00;
}

/* Book */
element["publication type"="book"] {
  color: #56B4E9;
}

/* Documentation */
element["publication type"="documentation"] {
  color: #D55E00;
}

#specify shadow ring around the publications that have a student author 
/* Student Author */
element["student author"="YES"] { #refers to the "student author" column in the dataset
  shadow-color: #8a2be2;
  shadow-opacity: 0.3;
  shadow-size: 1.5;
}
```
